Every behavior in the case follows from defaults being evaluated once, when the def statement runs.

brief.situation: You maintain slips.py at Tidewater Meal Kits (fictional). The packing-slip worker starts at 06:00 and runs all day. Since yesterday's release, each slip lists extras the customer never ordered, and later slips list more. Slips print at 14:00 for the 15:00 courier. It is 13:05.
handover: Yesterday's release added an optional extras list to slip_lines() so the gift service can pass its own notes.
Restarting the worker takes a minute and drops nothing.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look at the slips, change the code, run the tests, restart the worker, or ship the fix. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the team channel: why the slips grew, what you changed, and how you know.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: A default value is evaluated once, when def runs; extras=[] is one list object shared by every call that omits the argument, and append mutates it, so it accumulates for the life of the worker. Not memory, not data.
parts.modelAnswer: The default list lives on the function and every call appends to the same one.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Default to None and create a new list in the body. Copying on return still mutates the shared default; clearing at the start wipes a list the caller passed in (the gift notes); restarting only resets the shared list.
parts.modelAnswer: def slip_lines(order, extras=None): if extras is None: extras = [].

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: Tests after the last change: two calls in a row return independent results, and a caller's own list keeps its items.
parts.modelAnswer: Both tests pass on the shipped code.

scoring.modelReasoning: Slips that grow from call to call in a long-running worker point to state that outlives a call. extras=[] is evaluated once, when def runs, so every call that omits the argument appends to the same list. Restarting resets it only until the next calls. Returning a copy still grows the shared default, and extras.clear() wipes the gift service's own list. The fix is extras=None with a new list made inside, proved by one test for two calls in a row and one for a caller's own list.
